questions.question: Point 3 semicolon 2 has image negative 2 semicolon 3. Identify the transformation and give a check.
questions.expected_answer: The coordinates swapped and the new first coordinate changed sign, the pattern negative y semicolon x, so it is a rotation of 90 degrees anticlockwise about the origin. Check: both points are the square root of 13 from the origin.

questions.question: Point 1 semicolon negative 3 has image negative 2 semicolon 4. Identify the transformation completely.
questions.expected_answer: The distance from the origin changes, from the square root of 10 to the square root of 20, so it is a translation. Image minus original gives negative 3 and 7: a translation of 3 units left and 7 units up, rule x semicolon y maps to x minus 3 semicolon y plus 7.

questions.question: Why can the pair 4 semicolon 0 to negative 4 semicolon 0 fit two different transformations, and how is it resolved?
questions.expected_answer: Because y is zero, negating it changes nothing, so both reflection in the y-axis and rotation of 180 about the origin give the same image. A second point off the x-axis decides: its image will have y unchanged for the reflection and y negated for the rotation.
